question.text: 'Nilgiri Mid-Market AIF' has two named key persons: Ms. Radhika Swamy and Mr. Vikram Bhatnagar. The side letter with a pension fund LP contains a 'key-person event' clause. What is the TYPICAL operative consequence of a key-person event under such clauses?

answer.text: Immediate termination of the IMA without any LP vote

Suspension of the fund's investment/drawdown activity until investors approve a replacement key person or resolve the event; a continued unresolved event may lead to termination of the commitment period
The manager must personally compensate each LP for notional losses

explanation.text: The Logic: Consistent with Section 13.3 and 13.4.1 negotiation points, the typical key-person clause provides for a SUSPENSION of drawdowns/new investments upon a key-person event (death, disability, departure, breach of time-commitment), triggering a defined resolution period. If unresolved, the commitment period may be terminated and LPs may exit. Immediate IMA termination is too aggressive; fee waivers/personal indemnity aren't standard. The Trap: Immediate termination is the most draconian but not standard — gives LPs too much optionality. Fee waivers and personal compensation are not standard key-person consequences. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (PMS) doesn't have key-person clauses (it's typically a SMA or single portfolio manager). XIX-C uniquely tests this private-fund governance feature. Manager's Pro-Tip: Negotiate a 'cure period' of 90–180 days to find a replacement before suspension converts to commitment-period termination. Also, define 'key-person event' tightly — loose drafting lets LPs exit on any senior-staff departure.
